comments: Lewis in Pittsburgh; departs next day.
Meriwether Lewis departs in a 55-foot keelboat to begin the preliminary phase of the journey.
Lewis meets William Clark; they recruit the first members of the Corps of Discovery.
Winter training camp established on the east bank of the Mississippi River.
Official departure of the expedition up the Missouri River.
Final preparations completed before entering the wilderness.
First formal council held between the expedition and Native American tribes (Oto and Missouri).
Death and burial of Sergeant Charles Floyd, the only member to die on the mission.
Arrival at Mandan and Hidatsa villages; construction of Fort Mandan begins.
The 'permanent party' heads west while the keelboat returns to St. Louis with specimens.
Lewis reaches the five waterfalls of the Missouri, necessitating a difficult month-long portage.
The expedition crosses the Continental Divide.
Rest stop before the grueling trek through the Bitterroot Mountains.
The expedition reaches the Pacific Ocean.
Winter quarters established near the mouth of the Columbia River.
The Corps begins the return journey home.
Clark carves his name into the rock; it remains the only physical evidence on the trail.
The expedition arrives back at its starting point to a hero's welcome.
